newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian Authority frees top Hamas guerrilla.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian Authority frees top Hamas guerrilla.

text.p: Palestinian police freed a top leader of a military wing of Hamas on Monday in an apparent goodwill gesture towards the militant Islamic group, Hamas sources said.

They said Ibrahim al-Maqadmeh, who led a secret network within Hamas dedicated to attacks against Israel and weakening Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority, was freed on orders from the Palestinian president.
Palestinian security officials declined to comment on the report.

Sources in the Islamic Salvation Party, an affiliate of Hamas, said Maqadmeh's release followed heavy pressure by groups opposed to Israeli-PLO peace moves that had recently joined a national dialogue meeting with the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank town of Nablus.

Palestinians said Maqadmeh operated the "Secret Apparatus" network controlled by Hamas leaders abroad before he was arrested last year during a sweep against Hamas in the wake of suicide bombings in Israel in February and March.

The Palestinian Authority has since released most of the nearly 900 Hamas and Islamic Jihad supporters and activists rounded up in 1996. But at least 200 remain in jail, including many members of the secret network.
